metadata.title: Schema as Source of Truth.
metadata.source: Research: Prior Art on Schema-as-Source-of-Truth for Institutional AI Policy (2026-08-04)

beats.narration_text: Hey Liam — here's the question every AI-for-Teaching committee is sitting with right now.

props.command: Hey Claude — every instructor at a university needs the same AI policy in their syllabus. What could go wrong?
props.runningText: the committee wrote the policy in a Google Doc and sent it to fifty faculty to paste into fifty syllabi…
output: * Drift: N independent rewordings — nothing detects divergence
* Unauditability: compliance is a reading task, not a query
* AI-assisted rewriting makes both worse, not better

beats.act: the failure mechanism — drift and unauditability
beats.narration_text: Here is what happens when a policy lives as prose. A committee drafts it. Instructors paste it into syllabi — verbatim, paraphrased, or AI-assisted. Each copy is now independent. Semester to semester, each one drifts. N syllabi, N independent rewordings. Nothing detects divergence. Auditing whether any syllabus complies becomes a reading task across the whole corpus — not a query. Two compounding failures, both scaling with N: drift and unauditability.

manim.spec: one POLICY RECORD box at top; arrows down to five SYLLABUS boxes; phase 1 — connected diagram; phase 2 — syllabi drift to different colors showing N independent rewordings; phase 3 — DRIFT and UNAUDITABILITY labels in terracotta; cream background, warm-ink text

beats.act: the fix — one record, cascade update
beats.narration_text: The structural fix is one architectural decision. The policy is a record — typed fields, not prose. Every syllabus is a render of that record. Change one field. Every downstream syllabus gets the update automatically. Not N edits. One edit.

manim.spec: RECORD box at top with typed fields (permission_level, disclosure_format, approved_by); arrows to N SYLLABUS boxes; animate: one field changes (terracotta flash); all SYLLABUS boxes cascade-update; label: 1 EDIT → N RENDERS UPDATED; cream background

beats.act: prior art — four domains, same topology
beats.narration_text: This pattern has a name in four adjacent domains. Enterprise GRC: one versioned policy record, many rendered compliance documents, full audit trail. Technical writing: DITA conref — author once, reference everywhere, every rebuild propagates the update. Software engineering: docs-as-code — policy in git, every change a commit, every semester a tagged release. Legal document assembly: HotDocs — the template expert builds once, end users fill a form, the compliant document assembles automatically. Four domains. Same topology. One source, N derived outputs, automatic propagation.

manim.spec: four rows appearing sequentially; each row: domain label + ONE SOURCE box + arrows to three DERIVED boxes; rows: ENTERPRISE GRC / DITA CONREF / DOCS-AS-CODE / HOTDOCS; final frame: shared topology highlighted with ONE SOURCE → N DERIVED label; cream background, warm-ink text, terracotta accent

beats.act: the gap — higher ed tooling audit
beats.narration_text: An audit of the leading syllabus management platforms found no typed AI-disclosure field anywhere in the category. CourseLeaf SYL pulls structured curriculum metadata — course IDs, credits, outcomes — but policy content is a prose field. Watermark Concourse has a Policies tab: column A is policy name, column B is the description, entered as prose. No platform has a typed permission_level field, a disclosure_format field, or any structured AI-disclosure dimension. The pattern is established in four adjacent domains. Higher education's tooling has not caught up. A spreadsheet — one column per policy dimension — plus a documented render step is enough to start today.

lines: CourseLeaf / Watermark Concourse: policy content is a prose field. No typed dimensions.
Zero platforms: AI-disclosure schema field. Zero universities: AI policy as structured data.
Absence is the finding. A spreadsheet + render step is enough to start today.

beats.act: the meta-beat — the document about drift drifts
beats.narration_text: Here is the calibration finding. The source document that prompted this episode described Simple Syllabus as offering structured syllabus data, compliance checking, and institution-wide policy insertion. The live site says something softer. Structured syllabus data appears only in the pitch for Simple TA — a separate product. The main platform: centralized templates, reporting, accreditation compliance. No schema-level compliance checking. The document about prose drift exhibits prose drift. Caught by checking the source.

manim.spec: two-column layout: left panel DOCUMENT SAID with claim text; right panel LIVE SITE with different softer text; a not-equal symbol appears between panels; PROSE DRIFTS label appears in terracotta at bottom; cream background

beats.narration_text: The adoption argument. Enterprise GRC owns the one-record audit trail. DITA owns single-source reuse. Docs-as-code gives versioning free. HotDocs gives the non-technical wrapper. Applying this pattern to AI-disclosure policy in higher education is an adoption, not an invention. The lineage is citable. Name it. Use it.
